Article Title: Government set to halt sugarcane juice, B-heavy molasses diversion for ethanol
Article Text:
File photo: Sugarcane at a market, in Guwahati

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Government is set to disallow diversion of sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses for ethanol production in the 2026-27 ethanol supply year (ESY) starting November, amid an around 11% shortfall in sugar production from initial estimates for the 2025-26 sugar season and indications of a further decline in output due to drought in major sugarcane-growing states of Maharashtra and Karnataka.TOI has learnt that government will notify the decision soon, ahead of the start of the new ESY. While ethanol supply year runs from Nov 1 to Oct 31, sugar season in India runs from Oct 1 to Sep 30. Government specifies the quantity of sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses that can be diverted for ethanol production to meet the mandatory blending target for the green fuel in petrol.The move comes at a time when domestic sugar supplies remain tight. Mills diverted about 30 lakh tonnes of sugar, or around 10% of total output, for ethanol production during the sugar season that ended on September 30. The new sugar season began on October 1 with opening stocks of around 37.5 lakh tonnes, compared with nearly 50 lakh tonnes a year ago.Industry sources said there was no scope for allowing further diversion of sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses for ethanol, as ensuring adequate domestic sugar supplies remains a priority for both govt and mills.With the possibility of a fall in output in the current season, particularly in Maharashtra and Karnataka, government would prioritise sugar availability over additional diversion for ethanol.Disallowing the use of sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses for ethanol in 2026-27 would enable mills to produce more sugar from the available cane, helping augment domestic supplies and meeting consumption requirements.Government has said that the share of sugar diverted for ethanol has declined from around 12% in 2022-23 to around 9% in 2025-26. Besides, nearly three-fourths of ethanol produced in the country now comes from grains, particularly maize, reducing the dependence on sugar-based feedstock.“Meeting the demand for 20% ethanol blending in petrol won’t be an issue. With indications of millers getting a better price, it won’t be a problem for them either. Government would have to continue with the ban on exports and may have to allow more imports as well,” an industry analyst said.Sugar production in the 2025-26 season was hit by crop diseases, waterlogging and adverse weather in key producing states. Against the initial production estimate of around 343 lakh tonnes, output was estimated at around 306 lakh tonnes in August, including the quantity diverted for ethanol production.After accounting for the diversion to ethanol, net sugar production in 2025-26 was around 279 lakh tonnes, barely enough to meet the normative domestic consumption requirement of 280-285 lakh tonnes.
Article Summary: Government is set to disallow diversion of sugarcane juice, syrup and b-heavy molasses for ethanol production in the 2026-27 ethanol supply year (esy) the move comes amid an around 11% shortfall in sugar production from initial estimates for the 2025-26 sugar season.

Article Title: Jack Dorsey’s Bitchat taken off Indian app stores over law-and-order concerns: Report
Article Text:
Bitchat takedown puts Bluetooth messaging app

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Jack Dorsey’s Bluetooth-based messaging app Bitchat has been removed from Indian app stores following government intervention, putting the spotlight on concerns over decentralised communication. Government sources quoted by news agency PTI said on Tuesday that the app posed a law-and-order concern and therefore had to be taken down.The sources told PTI that Bitchat allows users to send messages through multiple Bluetooth “hops” without relying on conventional internet connectivity, raising concerns that it could be used to bypass restrictions imposed by authorities.“The government is duty-bound to maintain law and order,” sources said, adding that the app's ability to facilitate communication through Bluetooth was a concern.On proposals to restrict minors' access to social media, government sources said there was no such proposal under consideration. They pointed to Australia's experience, saying restrictions had not prevented children from accessing social media without accounts.The government is instead consulting industry representatives and experts, including those with expertise in psychology, sources said.“We have to find a better solution...when the right solution comes, we will bring it in front of you,” the sources said, stressing that a solution needed to be found.Apple removed Bitchat from the India App Store following a demand from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Dorsey said in an X post on Saturday.“Government of India officially removes Bitchat from the App Store,” Dorsey wrote, sharing a screenshot of Apple's App Review notice.The notice said the removal was “per demand from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)” because the app “includes content that is illegal in India”. It cited Section 69(A) of the Information Technology Act, 2000, under which the takedown demand was issued.Google has also removed the app from the Play Store in India, while Apple said it remained available in other territories selected by the developer. Its TestFlight version would also no longer be available for testing in India.Bitchat had previously faced government action in July. The Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C) had then directed GitHub to restrict access to its repositories, citing concerns that the decentralised network could enable communication during internet restrictions and make lawful detection more difficult.
Article Summary: Bitchat takedown puts bluetooth messaging app under spotlight. Apple removed bitchat from the india app store following a demand from the ministry of electronics and information technology (meity) google has also removed the app from the play store in india, while apple said it remained available in other territories selected by developer.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: Lpg consumption in sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (mt), compared to 2.9 mt during the same month a year earlier. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in july. Erratic monsoon conditions due to el nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.

Article Title: Travis Kelce’s 87 & Running Foundation makes a new move amid financial controversy as Ed and Donna Kelce enter the picture
Article Text:
Travis Kelce’s 87 & Running Foundation makes a new move amid financial controversy as Ed and Donna Kelce enter the picture (Image via Getty: Ed Kelce, Travis Kelce, and Donna Kelce)

Travis Kelce’s foundation continues youth work amid financial scrutiny

Donna Kelce joins students for special Chiefs experience

Ed Kelce connects family legacy with children

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Founded by Travis Kelce in 2015, 87 & Running Foundation aims to empower underserved youth by providing resources and opportunities in education, athletics, STEM, and the arts. Its “Ignition Lab” collaboration with the nonprofit organization Operation Breaththrough reflects the foundation’s mission.Through the Ignition Lab program, under-resourced teenagers from Kansas City neighborhoods can explore STEM and entrepreneurship with mentorship, equipment, and hands-on learning.Although 87 & Running Foundation’s Instagram account has seen no recent activity, its charitable work continues through initiatives like Operation Breakthrough’s Ignition Lab.According to the foundation’s website, the Ignition Lab program serves about 700 students daily. Young people have opportunities to learn, create, develop practical skills, and explore several pathways that could shape their future education and careers.87 & Running Foundation’s official Instagram account has not posted any content since January 2026. At the same time, social media fans raised money-laundering allegations against the foundation.According to The Arizona Republic, the foundation’s IRS filings reported raising about $1.5 million and spending roughly $1.1 million over a multi-year period [2021 to 2024].Only 41 cents of every dollar was reportedly directed to charitable programs.CharityWatch executive director, Laurie Styron, told The Arizona Republic that, “players and their managers need to stop using charities this way. Don’t get creative. Don’t look for loopholes.If you establish a charity, stop mixing in business interests or using friends to operate it. Do it the right way or don’t do it at all. There are a lot of ways for players to give back without founding their own charity.”Despite this growing tension, Travis Kelce’s foundation reportedly continued its work through the Ignition Lab program with Operation Breakthrough. Operation Breakthrough is a nonprofit organization that provides educational and developmental opportunities for children and families in Kansas City.Travis Kelce’s 87 & Running Foundation funds and powers its Ignition Lab program. The program gives 14- to 18-year-old teenagers access to resources that promote innovation, technical learning, and entrepreneurial thinking. This partnership expands 87 & Running Foundation’s financial support to create opportunities for young people.In August 2026, Operation Breakthrough expressed heartfelt gratitude to Travis Kelce for arranging an opportunity for Ignition Lab students. The students attended the Kansas City Chiefs’ first preseason game from Kelce’s suite at Arrowhead Stadium.The organization wrote on Instagram, “Talk about a suit surprise! Thanks to Travis Kelce, our Ignition Lab students experienced the Chiefs’ first preseason game from his suite at Arrowhead!”The post also mentioned that the students met Travis Kelce’s mother, Donna Kelce, during the outing. This experience gave participating students a heartfelt opportunity to enjoy a Chiefs game. It also helped them create lasting memories connected to their Kansas City community.The 87 & Running Foundation’s 2025 annual report speaks for the foundation’s continued charitable work.Their website also provides information about its programs and partnerships. However, their collaboration with Operation Breakthrough through Ignition Lat provides additional insight into the foundation's activities and its connection to the Kelce family. In particular, Travis Kelce’s father, Ed Kelce.On September 17, 2026, Operation Breakthrough shared a post on Instagram about Ed Kelce visiting. The father of NFL legends Jason and Travis Kelce read to first-grade students and showed them the cutest, rarest childhood photos of Jason and Travis.The organization wrote, “Storytime with a side of Kelce family throwbacks! Ed Kelce stopped by to read to our first graders, then gave them a peek at Travis and Jason when they were little, just like them! Thank you, Ed, for sharing your time and a little family history with our children!”Yesterday, it was Travis Kelce’s 37th birthday on October 5, 2026. The little angels at Operation Breakthrough sent warmest wishes for the Kansas City Chiefs tight end through an adorable Instagram reel.The organization collaborated on the post with 87 & Running Foundation and called it, “Little voices, BIG birthday wishes! Happy birthday, Travis! Sending lots of love from all of us at Operation Breakthrough.” This post marks the 87 & Running Foundation’s first social media update since January 2026.
Article Summary: 87 & running foundation aims to empower underserved youth by providing resources and opportunities in education, athletics, stem, and the arts. Its “ignition lab” collaboration with the nonprofit organization operation breaththrough reflects the foundation’s mission.

Article Title: Bombay HC to X: Remove video against Serum Institute, Adar Poonawalla
Article Text:
Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to take down a recent video uploaded by Yohan Tengra.





MUMBAI: Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to remove a video against Serum Institute of India Pvt Ltd and its CEO Adar Poonawalla that was uploaded by a social media influencer Yohan Tengra immediately after its June 5, 2023 order.Justice Gauri Godse of HC on Tuesday passed the order on SII and Poonawalla’s interim application in the pending defamation suit regarding content posted against the company and its COVID-19 vaccine. She also issued show-cause notices to Tengra, his organisation Anarchy for Freedom India, Ambar Koiri and TV 10 L.I.V.E, an online news portal, as to why action should not be taken for defying HC’s order. The notices are returnable on Oct 27.The application said Tengra and four defendants were restrained by the June 5, 2023 order from publishing or circulating defamatory videos and content. The same night Tengra uploaded a fresh video. On June 9, 2023, the plaintiffs issued a takedown notice to Google and X. Google complied but X refused, stating HC’s order was not issued against it.Advocate Karl Tamboly, for SII and Poonawalla, said videos uploaded were held to be unlawful by the June 5, 2023 order.Hence, videos and content of a like nature are also directed to be removed. He said in the absence of Tengra complying with HC’s direction, X is obligated to remove the objectionable content. Advocate Mayur Khandeparkar, for X, said the plaintiffs must initiate contempt proceedings against the defendants instead of waging a proxy battle with an intermediary.Justice Godse said it is undisputed that the objectionable content is still available with X. Tengra uploaded the fresh video not only in blatant defiance of HC’s injunction order “but he also states that he will not comply with the directions of the court and that he would not stop calling plaintiff no. 2 (Poonawalla) ‘a mass murderer’.”The judge noted there were no directions to X to remove the objectionable content and, thus, it cannot be held liable for the objectionable content not removed by the five defendants or for the new content uploaded by Tengra. Citing a Supreme Court judgment, she said even if an intermediary is exempt from liability for third-party information, necessary directions can be issued to remove the unlawful or prohibited content.Considering the “subsequent circumstance” of Tengra uploading the fresh video, Justice Godse said sufficient grounds are made out to direct X to “remove, delete or disable access” to the fresh video uploaded by Tengra.
Article Summary: Bombay high court has directed x corp to remove a video against serum institute of india pvt ltd and its ceo adar poonawalla. The video was uploaded by social media influencer yohan tengra immediately after its june 5, 2023 order. Justice gauri godse of hc on tuesday passed the order on an interim application in the pending defamation suit.

Article Title: India's factory growth hits 7 month high in September, thanks to demand and hiring boost
Article Text:
Factory growth hits 7-month high, PMI rises to 55.1

India’s manufacturing activity scaled up sharply in September, as stronger demand pushed up sales and production, while companies stepped up hiring and stock-building.The seasonally adjusted HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 55.1 in September, from 52.8 in August, marking the strongest improvement in the sector’s health in seven months. A PMI reading above 50 indicates expansion, while a reading below 50 signals contraction.The recovery in factory activity was supported by both domestic and overseas demand. Stronger new orders helped drive production higher, with demand across electronics, food, pharma and textiles taking total sales growth to its highest level since February.Export orders also gained momentum during the month, with manufacturers reporting increased business from clients in Brazil, Europe, the UAE and the US."India's factory sector ended the quarter on a firmer footing. The PMI rose to 55.1 in September, up from 52.8, as stronger domestic and overseas demand lifted sales and production. Hiring resumed at its fastest pace since May, and manufacturers became more optimistic about the months ahead," Pranjul Bhandari, chief India economist at HSBC, told PTI.The improvement in demand was accompanied by a renewed increase in factory employment.After a blip in August, job growth resumed in September, with the pace of employment expansion described by panellists as solid and the strongest since May.Manufacturers also became more confident about the months ahead. Output forecasts were upgraded during September, taking overall positive sentiment to a four-month high. The outlook was supported by a healthy pipeline of new enquiries and expectations that strong demand would continue.The expectation of higher future sales also prompted companies to increase their purchases of materials and build inventories. Overall buying activity expanded at a faster pace than in August."Companies bought more materials and built up stocks to prepare for anticipated sales. Finished goods inventories recorded their second-largest increase in nearly 12 years, signalling a clear shift from leaner stock levels," Bhandari said.Finished goods inventories rose for the third consecutive month. The increase was the second-fastest in 11-and-a-half years, behind July, as manufacturers actively accumulated stocks in anticipation of stronger demand.At the same time, companies faced quicker increases in input costs and selling prices. Despite the acceleration, the rates of inflation remained mild by historical standards.The September reading came as manufacturing activity regained momentum after the slower expansion recorded in August, with the PMI rising by more than two points during the month."Holdings of finished products increased for the third month in a row and at the second-fastest pace in 11-and-a-half years (behind July)," the report said.The HSBC India Manufacturing PMI is compiled by S&P Global based on responses from purchasing managers at around 400 manufacturers.
Article Summary: Factory growth hits 7-month high, pmi rises to 55.1. Stronger demand pushed up sales and production, while companies stepped up hiring and stock-building. Hiring resumed at its fastest pace since may, and manufacturers became more optimistic about the months ahead.

Article Title: Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses
Article Text:
Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses

Revenue growth draws investor attention

Huge infrastructure spending

Losses add to valuation questions

Customer concentration remains a risk

Anthropic has put a massive price tag on the AI boom, backing it with an equally heavy spending plan.The AI giant is heading towards a potential valuation of more than $2 trillion even as it plans $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations in the coming years.The company’s IPO prospectus, seen by Reuters, also shows just how quickly its business has grown. Anthropic’s revenue reportedly rose 12-fold in 2025, giving investors a strong growth story to weigh against its continuing losses and huge infrastructure commitments.The scale of its plans has also spilled into markets, with European technology shares rising 2.4% and the US chip index gaining 1.5%.For investors, Anthropic’s rapid expansion is a key part of the valuation story.Michael Field, chief equity strategist at Morningstar, Amsterdam, said the speed of the company’s growth stood out in the prospectus."If anything, the acceleration of the business is the biggest part of this release. Growing a big business can be difficult, but the prospectus stating that revenue grew by 12 fold in 2025 is truly remarkable."Field said the proposed valuation should be considered alongside the company’s sales."Obviously a $2 trillion valuation sounds outlandish, but when you break it down to a multiple of sales, likely to be around 18-20x, it sounds much more reasonable than the recent SpaceX IPO."Anthropic’s plans also show that the AI investment cycle is continuing to require substantial spending on infrastructure.Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB Platform, London, said the planned spending was positive for companies involved in semiconductors and AI infrastructure."This is positive for the AI trade, since it is fuelled by continued elevated levels of capex spend. The fact that Anthropic is planning on spending big on capex means that the capex cycle is not over yet. This is good news for semiconductor and AI infrastructure companies. I believe that if Anthropic had signalled a lower level of spending, this could have caused a wobble in the AI trade, since it would lead to fears about the sustainability of the AI trade as we move into Q4. "The prospectus puts rapid revenue growth alongside the large infrastructure commitments needed to support it.Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, London, said Anthropic’s expectations for AI’s economic impact appeared to have supported demand for European technology stocks."It's the vision and the projections to the extent to which Anthropic believes AI will be a game changer for economies around the world that seem to have lifted demand for European tech stocks."She also raised concerns over the company’s spending while it remains loss-making."There still will be niggles of concern among some about the huge sums that are projected to be spent even though it is making a loss. But that hasn't caused a flutter of general fear because, overall, there still seems to be a pretty hefty appetite for AI focused investments."Anthropic’s losses remain another factor in the debate around its proposed valuation.Field said the losses were a concern when considered against the company’s current revenue, growth rate and size. However, he said investors had already absorbed much of the spending story."The losses certainly are a concern. Particularly given the growth rate and the size relative to current revenues. It's unlikely to deter investors, however, with the spend story having been digested for some time now."He said the scale of planned investment also reflected management’s confidence in future demand."The key takeaway for investors is the confidence in the business and the AI strategy. Yes spend is high and growing, but management obviously feel the growth rate inherent in demand is sufficiently attractive to keep spending, hence why they are coming to market and demanding a top-dollar valuation."Anthropic’s revenue growth is another area attracting attention, particularly because a significant share reportedly comes from a small number of customers.Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, London, said the company’s revenue growth had become the main focus despite its spending plans. "Massive spending would normally have investors running for the hills, but what's capturing the market's attention is Anthropic's stellar revenue growth, up 12-fold in 2025. Admittedly, AI is moving at such a rapid pace that last year’s sales achievements relate to technology that is already outdated. "Anthropic’s IPO plans therefore bring together rapid revenue growth, continuing losses and a huge infrastructure commitment. The company is seeking a valuation of more than $2 trillion while planning $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations.
Article Summary: Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses. Revenues reportedly rose 12-fold in 2025, giving investors a strong growth story to weigh against its continuing losses and huge infrastructure commitments. European technology shares rose 2.4% and the us chip index gained 1.5%.

Article Title: Google CEO Sundar Pichai announces EmbeddingGemma 2 model; says it is company’s first open, natively multimodal embedding model
Article Text:
Announcing the new model, Google CEO

Sundar Pichai

said: “Introducing EmbeddingGemma 2, a new open multimodal model that sets the standard for on-device efficiency.

- our first open, natively multimodal embedding model

- handles text, code, image, video, and audio tasks within a lightweight, modular 740M parameter form factor

- ideal for offline, privacy-first RAG when paired with Gemma 4

- outperforms some specialist models more than twice its size

Weights available now on Hugging Face.”

EmbeddingGemma 2: Key capabilities

Native multimodal retrieval: Unlocks search across text, code, images, video, and audio directly in a shared 768-dimensional vector space.

Superior code understanding: Significantly outperforms EmbeddingGemma 1 on code search and technical retrieval, making it ideal for local codebase indexing and agentic code search.

Modular memory footprint: Selectively load only the encoders you need at runtime: 270M (text/code), 440M (text + vision), 570M (text + audio), or 740M (full multimodal), all projecting into the same compatible vector space.

Flexible vector storage: Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) enables dynamic truncation from 768 dimensions down to 128 dimensions, cutting vector database storage requirements while retaining much of the original quality. For instance, at 256 dimensions, most of the full quality of the original embedding on text and code is retained and about 95% on image, video, and speech retrieval

How it works

Text and code (270M base): An adapted Gemma 4 decoder with an 8,192-token context window.

Vision (+170M): A vision encoder that processes images, visual documents (PDFs, slides, charts), and video frames.

Audio (+300M): A dedicated speech and sound encoder that directly ingests raw audio.

Modular loading: You only load what you need. Run text-only at 270M parameters, add vision for 440M parameters, or load the full multimodal model at 740M parameters.

Shared tokenizer & audio encoder with Gemma 4: When paired with Gemma 4 in an on-device RAG pipeline, both models share the same text tokenizer and audio encoder architecture, reducing the total memory footprint.

Google has launched EmbeddingGemma 2, an open multimodal embedding model for devices. The launch comes a year after the company introduced EmbeddingGemma for developers last year. For those unaware, an embedding model is a machine learning tool that turns complex data like words, sentences, images, or audio into a list of numbers called a vector. Built on the Gemma 4 architecture and released under a commercially permissive Apache 2.0 license, EmbeddingGemma 2 has 740 million parameters, making it optimal for on-device inference. It can help find a specific video clip from a voice memo, or search through hours of audio recordings based on a text query, all processed by a single, natively multimodal model.EmbeddingGemma 2 is designed to provide a single, compact open model released under the Apache 2.0 license, delivering exceptional multimodal performance for its size. Based on Gemma 4, this sub-1B model maps text, code, images, video, and audio into a unified 768-dimensional space. Its modular architecture can scale from 270M parameters for text and code up to 740M parameters for all modalities. Key capabilities of the EmbeddingGemma include:Google says that all inputs are processed through the shared backbone and their resulting embeddings occupy the same dimensional space:
Article Summary: Google launches embeddinggemma 2, an open multimodal embedding model for devices. Based on gemma 4, this sub-1b model maps text, code, images, video, and audio into a unified 768-dimensional space. Built on the gemma4 architecture and released under a commercially permissive apache 2.0 license.

Article Title: Scientists build ‘mind-reading’ AI program that can tell what you are thinking and recreates photos with striking accuracy
Article Text:
Major leap from grainy predecessors

How scientists solved data problem with a dual-translation ‘encoder’

Irani explained how the algorithmic framework generated its own training data:

A group of Israeli scientists have engineered an advanced artificial intelligence (AI) system called Brain-IT that can interpret what a person is picturing in his mind and then using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data, reconstruct those mental photos with remarkable precision. Detailed in a research submission to the International Conference on Learning Representations, the system yields visual outputs that closely reflect the real images viewed by subjects across both structural layouts and semantic meanings.The visual recreations demonstrated by the team range from basic street stop signs to intricate scenes like a tomato-and-olive pizza that captures the exact slice count envisioned by the viewer, essentially acting virtually like a digital replica of internal cognitive thought.While AI brain-decoding projects have surfaced before, Brain-IT establishes a dramatically higher benchmark for speed and fidelity. In 2017 (Purdue University), early models developed in Indiana could infer the general category of an image a participant imagined but the visual recreations were noticeably blurry and indistinct.In 2022 (Japan), researchers applied diffusion-style architectures to generate sharper approximations, though the framework depended heavily on intermediate text-to-image translation.Brain-IT has been developed under the direction of Michal Irani at the Weizmann Institute of Science, and mirrors target images with minute accuracy while completing the analysis process within just one hour, cutting down significantly from multi-hour processing runs required by previous systems.A major challenge in neuroimaging research is the physical and financial limitation of gathering human data. To train the architecture, researchers gathered records of eight subjects observing more than 70,000 pictures inside fMRI machines. As eight individuals represent a modest cohort for training frontier AI, the team bypassed the need for round-the-clock machine sessions by creating an “encoder” shortcut that enabled bidirectional translation.“We realized that by translating back and forth – from a random image that had never been viewed in an fMRI machine, to a predicted brain scan, and then back to the image we started with – the models would effectively build themselves a massive dataset. In this way, during training, the models would learn to generate scans that encode images effectively, even though those fMRI scans had never actually been performed.”Through this dual-decoding workflow, the system pinpointed 128 functional brain regions, including uncovering a mixture of familiar zones alongside newly identified areas, that carry out comparable visual processing tasks across different people. Certain clusters responded predictably to culinary imagery, others ignited when subjects viewed athletics and distinct neural pathways corresponded to indoor versus outdoor settings.The researchers see practical applications for the breakthrough, especially as an assistive communication system for paralysed patients who have lost physical speech or movement.
Article Summary: Israeli scientists have developed an advanced artificial intelligence (ai) system called brain-it. It can interpret what a person is picturing in his mind and then using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fmri) data, reconstruct those mental photos with remarkable precision.

Article Title: In 2021, Elon Musk put up $100 million for carbon removal; five years later, 136 teams have removed 243,552 tonnes of CO₂ and raised $3.3 billion
Article Text:
Elon Musk 's $100m carbon-removal challenge

136 teams removed 243,552 tonnes of CO₂

The challenge helped attract $3.3bn in capital

875 patents filed during the competition

Mati Carbon won the $50m grand prize

In 2021, the Musk Foundation put up $100 million for a global competition aimed at finding ways to remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and oceans and store it durably. The XPRIZE Carbon Removal competition ran for four years, drew 1,334 registered teams from more than 88 countries and helped turn carbon removal into a credible, investable sector. According to XPRIZE's Post-Prize Impact Report, released in April 2026, the 136 Distinguished Teams collectively removed 243,552 tonnes of CO₂ over the course of the competition, and participating companies raised more than $3.3 billion in capital during and after the prize period. The report also points to hundreds of companies created, thousands of skilled jobs generated and 875 patents filed.XPRIZE announced the $100 million competition on February 8, 2021, with funding from Elon Musk and the Musk Foundation. It officially launched on Earth Day, April 22, 2021, when team registration opened. The challenge asked teams worldwide to develop technologies that remove CO₂ from the atmosphere or oceans and store it durably and sustainably, while showing a credible path to gigatonne-scale removal.The competition ran through Earth Week 2025, and XPRIZE describes it as the largest incentive competition in history. Teams worked across four removal pathways: air, rocks, ocean and land.According to the impact report, the 136 Distinguished Teams collectively removed 243,552 tonnes of CO₂ over the course of the competition. They also sold 9,475,438 tonnes of carbon credits, a figure that includes future deliveries of tonnes removed. Buyers included Microsoft, Google, Salesforce, Stripe, Shopify, Meta, McKinsey, BCG and JPMorgan.The two figures measure different things. The 243,552 tonnes were actually removed during the competition, while the larger credit figure also counts tonnes sold for delivery in the future.The removal total remains small against the problem it targets. Global CO₂ emissions run at roughly 37 billion tonnes a year, so the tonnes removed during the competition amount to far less than 0.001% of one year's emissions. XPRIZE's argument is that the competition built a pipeline of demonstrated solutions that can now move from pilots towards commercial deployment. It also acknowledges that carbon markets face headwinds in 2026.Participating companies raised more than $3.3 billion in capital during and following the prize period, which XPRIZE describes as a 33-fold return relative to the $100 million purse. The money is capital raised by the companies themselves, not money returned to Musk or the XPRIZE Foundation, and XPRIZE's report does not specify which participating companies the figure covers.XPRIZE says the competition's structured milestones and third-party validation led to a 464% increase in average deal size and a 176% increase in the number of unique investors backing competing teams. More than half of the 1,334 registered teams were founded after the prize launched, and dozens are now running pilot projects or commercial deployments across six continents.Teams filed 875 patents during the four-year prize period from 2021 to 2025, which XPRIZE says is a 958% increase in the annual rate of patent filings. XPRIZE also estimates that the $100 million purse helped catalyse more than $300 million in research and development that might not otherwise have happened.The technologies ranged from engineered systems that capture carbon directly from air or oceans to approaches that use natural processes involving rocks, soil and organic waste.XPRIZE announced the winners on April 23, 2025, selecting them from 20 finalists across 11 countries. Each winning team removed more than 1,000 net tonnes of CO₂ in the competition's final year.The $50 million grand prize went to Mati Carbon, which spreads finely crushed basalt on agricultural land in India to accelerate a natural weathering process that permanently removes atmospheric CO₂. XPRIZE says the approach also benefits smallholder farmers through improved soil health, reduced agricultural inputs and increased income.NetZero, a French biochar company operating in Brazil, received $15 million as first runner-up. Vaulted Deep, a US waste-management company that stores unusable organic waste deep underground, received $8 million. UNDO Carbon, which uses enhanced rock weathering in Scotland and Canada, received $5 million. XFACTOR awards of $1 million each went to Planetary, for ocean alkalinity enhancement, and Project Hajar, a partnership between Aircapture and 44.01 that captures CO₂ from the air and mineralises it underground in the United Arab Emirates. Across the competition, $5 million also went to student teams and $15 million to milestone awards for early-stage demonstrations.With the competition over, XPRIZE says the field has moved beyond technical validation and early demonstrations towards commercial readiness. The next test is whether stronger demand for carbon removal emerges to scale these technologies to the level scientists say will be needed.
Article Summary: Elon musk's $100m carbon-removal challenge helped attract $3.3bn in capital. 136 teams removed 243,552 tonnes of co₂ over the course of the competition. They also sold 9,475,438 tonnes of carbon credits, a figure that includes future deliveries of tonnes removed.

Article Title: Xbox secures exclusive GTA 6 streaming rights ahead of launch: All details
Article Text:
Image via Rockstar Games

A cloud route to PC

A counter to PlayStation's marketing push

Timing: Streaming limits arrive in November

Microsoft’s Xbox has reportedly landed exclusive cloud streaming rights for Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6), a move that could give PC gamers access to the highly anticipated title at launch even though Rockstar Games has yet to announce a PC version. According to a report by The Verge, Xbox Cloud Gaming will be the only cloud service allowed to stream GTA 6 when the game launches. The duration of the reported exclusivity agreement remains unclear. The report said Xbox CEO Asha Sharma told employees during an all-hands meeting that Microsoft was preparing to do something around GTA 6 that “no other platform holder is doing.” Sources familiar with the company’s plans told The Verge that the comment referred to Xbox securing exclusive streaming rights for the game.The biggest effect may be on PC players. Rockstar has not announced a PC version of GTA 6, and The Verge said the deal lets Xbox pitch its cloud service to PC players who would otherwise need an Xbox Series X/S or a PS5. That means the game could be playable on PC in November through cloud streaming, though it would not be a native PC release.For anyone weighing a console purchase just for GTA 6, the deal could provide another way in.For Microsoft, it is a chance to promote Xbox Cloud Gaming on a title that is expected to dominate the holiday season.GTA 6 is set to launch on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. PlayStation holds the marketing deal for the game. Many ads say it "plays best on PS5." The reported streaming exclusivity gives Xbox its own GTA 6 selling point after that PlayStation-led campaign.The report lands as Xbox Cloud Gaming is about to change. The Verge reports that starting in November, monthly cloud gaming access will be capped at 15 hours for Game Pass Ultimate subscribers, 10 hours for Premium subscribers and five hours for Essential subscribers. Those limits could matter for a game as large as GTA 6, where long sessions are common.To offset the caps, players will be able to buy bundles of streaming hours without needing a Game Pass subscription. Microsoft has not announced prices. One unconfirmed rumour puts the cost at $5.99 for 25 streaming hours.
Article Summary: Gta 6 set to launch on playstation 5 and xbox series x|s. Xbox cloud gaming will be the only cloud service allowed to stream the game. Starting in november, monthly cloud gaming access will be capped at 15 hours for game pass ultimate subscribers, 10 hours for premium subscribers and five hours for essential.

Article Title: AI Data Security : Everyone wants an AI agent but almost nobody is asking where the data goes
Article Text:
Start with some very simple questions

“Trust us” isn’t enough

AI needs to earn our trust

By: Krish Ramineni, Co-founder & CEO, Fireflies.ai

Everyone wants an AI agent right now. We want AI that can prepare us for meetings, answer emails, search through our work, update the CRM and eventually just get things done for us. That’s where this is going. AI is moving from something you open when you need help to something that is always there, working alongside you. Less like another tool and more like an AI teammate.But there’s one question we’re not asking enough: Where does all that data go?Because the more useful your AI teammate becomes, the more it needs to know about you and your company. If it’s preparing you for a meeting, it might need access to your calendar, past meetings and documents. If it’s writing an email, it might need access to your inbox. If it’s updating your CRM, it needs access to customer information. And if you eventually want it doing work for you all day, it may need access to almost everything you use at work. The most useful AI teammate may also be the one that knows the most about your work. That’s why security matters so much.Before a company gives an AI access to its information, it should know what happens to that information. Is our data being used to train AI models? Where is it stored? How long is it kept? Who can see it? Can we delete it? Can we control what the AI has access to? Can we see what actions it has taken? And what happens when another AI company or model is involved?These sound like basic questions. But as we give AI access to more of our work, they become incredibly important.Security shouldn’t be something companies think about after they buy an AI product. It should be part of deciding which AI products they trust in the first place.Microsoft says Copilot follows a company’s existing permissions and that its business data isn’t used to train its foundation models. Google says Gemini for Workspace follows existing Workspace protections and doesn’t use customer data to train its generative AI models without permission. Zoom says it doesn’t use customer communications to train its own or third-party AI models. There’s a reason companies are starting to make these promises much clearer. Security is becoming part of the product.This becomes even more important when AI has access to conversations. Think about what gets discussed in meetings: customers, employees, hiring, strategy, financials and plans that may never be written down anywhere else. Companies should know exactly what happens to that information. At Fireflies, for example, we don’t use customer meeting content to train AI models. We require third-party vendors handling meeting content to follow zero-data-retention requirements. We also maintain SOC 2 Type II, GDPR and HIPAA compliance. “Trust us” isn’t a security policy. Companies should be able to understand where their data goes, who can access it and what controls they have over it.Banning AI isn’t the answer. Some companies may look at these risks and decide the safest thing to do is block AI altogether. I don’t think that solves the problem. People are already using AI to write, research, prepare for meetings and get work done faster. If their company blocks these tools, some employees will simply use personal accounts or other apps the company doesn’t know about. Now the company has even less control over where its data is going.A better approach is to give employees AI products the company has actually reviewed and approved and then set clear rules around what those products can see and what they’re allowed to do.This gets even more important as AI starts taking action. There’s a big difference between drafting an email and sending it. There’s a difference between suggesting a CRM update and making the change. There’s a difference between finding a document and sharing it with someone.The more AI can do on your behalf, the more control you need over what it’s allowed to do.For the last few years, everyone has been focused on making AI smarter. Can it answer better questions? Can it understand more? Can it do more work?Those things still matter. But as AI becomes more deeply connected to our work, there’s another question that matters just as much: Can we trust it?Today, a company might use AI to take meeting notes. Tomorrow, that same AI teammate could prepare you for meetings, search your email and Slack, update your CRM, follow up with customers and take care of work across dozens of apps.Every time we give it another ability, we’re also giving it more access. And that means companies need to know that their AI teammate is looking at the right information, for the right reason, and doing only what it has permission to do.The goal isn’t just to build AI that knows more. It’s to build AI that we can trust to do more.
Article Summary: “trust us” isn’t enough; ai needs to earn our trust, says krish ramineni. Companies should be able to understand where their data goes, who can access it and what controls they have over it. The more ai can do on your behalf, the more control you need over what it’s allowed to do.

Article Title: Claude Code creator Boris Cherny shares what not to miss while giving prompt to Claude; says: There's no secret to ...
Article Text:
Anthropic’s Boris Cherny reveals what matters on prompting AI today

The prompt that caught attention

Anthropic’s Claude Code creator, Boris Cherny has offered a simple piece of advice to users who are trying to get better results from AI models. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) Cherny asked the users to talk to Claude the same way they would talk to a coworker. As per Cherny users no longer need highly structured and very detailed prompts for most tasks, as modern AI models are increasingly capable of figuring out how to achieve a goal on their own. In the post shared on X, Cherny revealed that he was surprised that people were surprised by the way he prompts Claude. “Talk to Claude the way you would a coworker. There's no secret to prompting. There's no need to be overly scaffolded or prescriptive for most tasks. Give Claude a goal, and it will figure it out,” he wrote.Cherny contrasted the current approach with the early days of Claude's Sonnet 3.5 models, when the exact wording of a prompt mattered a great deal. Today's models, he suggested, need less hand-holding on the "how" and more clarity about the "what."He said it is now much more important to communicate three things to the model:1. What you want it to do2. How much effort you want it to spend3. How it should verify that it did the right thingThe comments align with advice Cherny has shared in public discussions, where he has argued that many users make the mistake of over-specifying every step instead of clearly defining the desired outcome.Modern AI models are often better used by describing the goal and success criteria rather than dictating a rigid sequence of actions.Alongside his comments, Cherny shared an example of a prompt he uses with Claude.In the example, he asked the AI to create an interactive artefact about a recent podcast episode on Home Depot's acquisition strategy. Rather than providing detailed step-by-step instructions, he described the end goal: a visually rich, interactive experience that highlights key business lessons.The prompt asked Claude to make the output “beautiful and interactive,” focus on business wisdom from the episode, use extensive reasoning and iteration, and incorporate elements such as watercolour illustrations, historical photographs and visual storytelling inspired by publications such as The New Yorker and The New York Times.Notably, the prompt emphasised the desired outcome and quality bar rather than prescribing a detailed process, reflecting the prompting philosophy Cherny advocates.
Article Summary: Anthropic’s boris cherny reveals what matters on prompting ai today. “talk to claude the way you would a coworker. There's no secret to prompting. Give claude a goal, and it will figure it out,” he wrote.

Article Title: TP-Link Systems Inc issues public statement; says: Stop calling us a 'Chinese company', we are an American company and no threat to …
Article Text:
TP-Link Systems Inc issues public statement; says: Stop calling us a 'Chinese company'

Here’s what TP-Link said

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier recently filed a civil lawsuit against Wi-Fi router manufacturer TP-Link. The lawsuit accuses the company of misleading Florida consumers about its products’ security and its ties to China. In the 59-page lawsuit, Uthmeier said that Chinese state-sponsored hackers exploited TP-Link routers sitting in American living rooms. “Many of those models cannot update themselves automatically, and TP-Link has stopped supporting them”. “They also told Floridians they had split from China and that they build U.S. products in Vietnam. That is fiction. Research and manufacturing remain rooted in China. Less than 1% of the parts in that Vietnam plant actually come from Vietnam,” he further added.TP-Link has now responded to the lawsuit, issuing an official statement saying that it is a US company, and not a ‘Chinese’ firm. “TP-Link Systems is a U.S. company that complies with U.S. privacy and data protection laws,” the company said adding “Any claims that our products present a threat to user security or grant unauthorized network access to foreign governments are baseles”.In a press release, Steve Kovsky, corporate affairs officer for TP-Link Systems Inc.said “The coordinated lawsuits are built on false premises. They do nothing to advance national security while unfairly penalizing an industry-leading U.S. company”.“We stand fully behind the security of our products, the integrity of our company and our people, and our commitment to serving the best interests of our customers in the United States and globally. We look forward to refuting these baseless allegations in court,” Kovsky added.In the release, the company further stated”: “For months, California-based TP-Link Systems has provided state regulators with clear, verifiable documentation demonstrating two fundamental facts: TP-Link Systems devices sold in the U.S. are manufactured in Vietnam and TP-Link Systems is an independent, U.S. company that is not owned or controlled by any foreign government.”“Any claims that our products present a threat to user security or grant unauthorized network access to foreign governments are baseless. TP-Link Systems is a U.S. company that complies with U.S. privacy and data protection laws. We perform comprehensive security testing and rely on trusted third-party security labs for additional scrutiny to ensure our products meet the highest security standards and are recognized as among the most secure on the market. We meet or exceed all industry best practices for monitoring and preventing vulnerabilities and actively support our customers to mitigate any issues that occur as they are identified. We do not, and will not, share customer network data with foreign governments or unauthorized third parties”.
Article Summary: Tp-link systems inc issues public statement; says: stop calling us a 'chinese company' florida attorney general james uthmeier recently filed a civil lawsuit against wi-fi router manufacturer tp-link. The lawsuit accuses the company of misleading consumers about its products’ security and its ties to china.

Article Title: In 1992, Larry Ellison shattered his elbow in a bicycle crash; after a UC Davis surgeon repaired it, the Oracle co-founder gave $5 million to help others with bone and muscle disorders
Article Text:
Oracle founder Larry Ellison

Record-setting donation made by Larry Ellison

What the money built

A serious bicycle accident suffered by Oracle CEO Larry Ellison in the early 1990s ultimately resulted in a $5 million donation that helped expand research into bone and muscle disorders at UC Davis, according to the university. The Oracle co-founder's gift helped build a musculoskeletal research and care program at UC Davis that is still part of the university's orthopaedic identity. Ellison, the co-founder and longtime chief executive of Oracle, shattered his elbow in a bicycle crash in 1992. The injury was treated by Michael Chapman, an orthopaedic surgeon at UC Davis, who successfully reconstructed the damaged joint. Following the surgery, Ellison donated $5 million to support musculoskeletal research and patient care at the university.The gift helped establish what became the Lawrence J. Ellison Musculoskeletal Research Center, where physicians, surgeons and scientists work on research aimed at preventing and treating musculoskeletal disorders. According to UC Davis, the centre focuses on conditions affecting bones, muscles and joints, bringing together experts from multiple disciplines.UC Davis announced the pledge in September 1995, when it reported record private giving of $41.5 million for fiscal year 1994-95.That was a 39 percent increase over the $29.8 million raised the year before. Ellison, then CEO of Oracle, made the largest single gift of the year. The $5 million pledge was meant to create three endowed chairs and a musculoskeletal institute in the School of Medicine."Mr. Ellison's generosity in particular will help sustain our nationally recognized expertise and care for patients with bone or muscle diseases," said Gerald S. Lazarus, then dean of the School of Medicine. The School of Medicine received $12.7 million in private support that year, an 88 percent increase. The university said this was the largest amount ever given to an academic unit on the campus.The Ellison center brings together physicians, surgeons and basic scientists. They study the prevention and treatment of what UC Davis calls "crippling and painful musculoskeletal disorders."A 2011 UC Davis Health profile described the center as part of a broader orthopaedic and sports medicine program. Its specialists have served as team doctors for the NBA's Sacramento Kings for more than two decades. The same program provides care for Olympic-level athletes, the national soccer program and UC Davis teams. US News & World Report ranked UC Davis among the nation's best hospitals for orthopaedics.Paul Di Cesare, then chair of orthopaedic surgery, said the program uses the same advanced techniques for professionals and ordinary patients. "We use those same modalities and treatments for the average athlete and the weekend warrior," he said.
Article Summary: Oracle co-founder larry ellison shattered his elbow in a bicycle crash in 1992. He donated $5 million to support musculoskeletal research and patient care at uc davis. The gift helped establish what became the lawrence j. ellison musculoskeleton research center. The center focuses on conditions affecting bones, muscles and joints.

Article Title: A diverse product mix and new markets to match at INNOPROM. India
Article Text:
Disclaimer - The above content is non-editorial, and TIL hereby disclaims any and all warranties, expressed or implied, relating to it, and does not guarantee, vouch for or necessarily endorse any of the content.

At INNOPROM. India, the discussion about diversifying trade took on a tangible form. In a single exhibition hall, Russian excavators and truck cranes stood alongside glass insulators for high-voltage lines, endoprostheses, industrial warning systems, and materials for road construction.These products have different markets, different buyers, and different paths to market. But they share one question: what new connections can be built between Russian manufacturers and India’s growing market?The inaugural edition of the industrial trade fair was held between September 9–11 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. The Russian Export Center brought a business mission of 23 companies to the exhibition. The delegation's geographic reach stretched from Moscow and St. Petersburg to the Chelyabinsk, Samara, Tomsk, Novosibirsk, and Sverdlovsk regions. What defined the mission was the number of industries represented — sectors that had rarely appeared together in a single narrative about Russia–India economic cooperation.Russia and India have long described their relationship as a Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership. In recent years, that partnership has been accompanied by a sharp increase in trade: bilateral trade reached $68.7 billion* in the 2024/25 financial year, while the first half of 2026 showed another 8% increase. By 2030, the two countries aim to bring bilateral trade to $100 billion.Russian exports are still dominated by oil and petroleum products, fertilizers, coal, vegetable oils, and precious metals. India, for its part, supplies Russia with pharmaceuticals, chemicals, steel, and seafood, although the trade balance remains heavily skewed. The challenge, therefore, is broader than simply increasing the total value of trade: the relationship needs more product categories, more companies, and more joint projects on both sides.The exhibition floor at INNOPROM. India offered a glimpse of what that expansion could look like. SDM (United Machinery Group) presented road-construction machinery; Sinara Transport Machines showcased solutions for high-speed railways; UMEK presented high-voltage insulators; and CITO displayed endoprostheses and trauma-care products.Nearby, Indian partners were introduced to tire-pressure monitoring systems from RD Group, industrial warning equipment from Armtel, and asphalt-concrete modifiers from Stilobit.An assortment like this is difficult to reduce to a single sales pitch. Each solution has its own procurement, testing, and approval cycle. That is why the value of an industrial exhibition begins where the presentation ends: standing beside an actual product, buyers and engineers can discuss load requirements, standards, after-sales service, localisation, and potential pilot applications.The day after INNOPROM. India closed, the main program of the 18th BRICS Summit began in New Delhi, running from September 12–13. India placed four themes at the heart of its BRICS chairmanship: resilience, innovation, cooperation, and sustainable development. As the grouping marked its 20th anniversary this year, the discussion about its future increasingly focused on implementation and practical cooperation. The economic agenda included tools closer to the daily needs of companies, while BRICS members agreed on a framework for cooperation on logistics and supply chains. The Indian chairmanship also introduced the BRICS SME Cooperation Portal, a network of incubators, and an initiative to support startups. At the BRICS Business Forum, Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for identifying the main trade barriers within the grouping and creating new business partnerships among companies each year.For Russian and Indian businesses, this represents a shift in scale. Supply-chain resilience does not begin with an abstract diagram. It starts with a handful of practical questions: where to find a supplier, how to verify that a product meets local requirements, which route to use for shipping, and whom to contact after delivery. For a smaller manufacturer, navigating that process alone can be difficult. A business platform, a reliable local operator, and the opportunity to demonstrate a working product can therefore shorten the distance between initial interest and substantive negotiations.On September 11, ahead of the summit’s official opening, Narendra Modi and Vladimir Putin discussed implementation of the Programme of Economic Cooperation till 2030. The leaders also highlighted the first INNOPROM. India and then visited the exhibition, where they spoke with participants.The exhibition ended on September 11, but the business infrastructure created around it did not disappear with the exhibition stands. On August 21, India’s first permanent “Made in Russia” national pavilion opened in Navi Mumbai1. Its first exhibitors presented food products, beverages, and consumer goods. The Indian operator, RAI FAMILY CORP LLP, is responsible for promotion, logistics, and working with local sales channels.New Delhi and Navi Mumbai are clearly addressing different parts of the same challenge. At INNOPROM. India, an engineer or procurement specialist can examine machinery and industrial solutions. At the pavilion, a buyer or retailer can sample a product and discuss supplying it to a retail network. The common denominator is the “Made in Russia” national brand program for promoting Russian products, implemented by the Russian Export Center. The ecosystem combines voluntary certification with exhibitions, business missions, and permanent platforms abroad.Contracts ultimately depend on price, quality, standards, and delivery terms. Now that dialogue has a clearer address and a more defined sequence: a manufacturer can begin with a business mission, continue with technical discussions, provide samples, test demand through a local operator, and prepare a commercial proposal for a specific partner.The headline figures in Russia–India trade have been built on products the two countries have traded for years. The next chapter will be visible in other indicators: the number of Indian companies using Russian industrial solutions and the number of Russian brands becoming familiar to local consumers.September 2026 has brought these efforts together across three platforms — INNOPROM. India, the BRICS Summit, and the “Made in Russia” national pavilion in Navi Mumbai.References:
Article Summary: Russia and india have long described their relationship as a special and privileged strategic partnership. Bilateral trade reached $68.7 billion* in the 2024/25 financial year. By 2030, the two countries aim to bring bilateral trade to $100 billion. On august 21, india’s first permanent “made in russia” national pavilion opened in navi mumbai.

Article Title: Florida man arrested after placing virus on woman’s computer, sharing private info in more than 100 TikTok videos
Article Text:
Florida man published more than 100 videos on Tik Tok

Woman alleged a virus was placed on her computer

Investigators also examined alleged location tracking

Police seized electronic devices

Earlier stalking allegations were dropped

Prosecutors revived the computer case

A 36-year-old Florida man was arrested after investigators accused him of gaining unauthorised access to a woman’s computer and posting private information involving women in more than 100 TikTok videos. Mark Stephen Asea of Port St. Lucie was booked into the St Lucie County Jail on September 30 on a felony computer-access charge, with his bond set at $35,000. The case followed an investigation into allegations involving at least two women, including claims that Asea had remotely accessed a computer, obtained passwords and private material, and discussed personal information in his online videos. Investigators also examined claims involving location data, purchases and private conversations. Asea’s earlier stalking allegations were dropped, but prosecutors later revived the computer-related case in September.The investigation centred partly on Asea’s TikTok account, where police say he published more than 100 videos involving one of the women. According to the police affidavit cited by local and national media, some of the videos allegedly contained details about the woman’s personal life and information that investigators believed he should not have had access to.Detectives reviewed videos in which Asea discussed information including a password, phone or device details, purchases and location-related information. The woman told investigators that some of the information had been shared privately and questioned how Asea had obtained it.Asea has presented himself online using descriptions including “grey hat hacker” and “demonologist”. His online profiles have also used terms such as “cybersecurity engineer”, according to reporting based on the police investigation.A separate allegation involved another woman who told investigators that Asea had previously helped her remotely with a computer problem. According to the affidavit, the woman had allowed Asea to access her computer remotely in October 2025 while he helped troubleshoot an application. She later became concerned after allegedly learning that he had installed a programme or virus that could allow continued access without her knowledge or permission.The woman also told police that a photograph from a private conversation later appeared in one of Asea’s TikTok videos. Investigators examined the circumstances surrounding the image and the alleged access to her electronic device. The computer-related allegation ultimately became the focus of the criminal charge filed against Asea in September.Police also investigated allegations that Asea had access to information about a woman’s location. According to the affidavit, detectives reviewed online material in which Asea allegedly discussed GPS information connected to the woman’s phone. The investigation examined whether he had obtained information that would allow him to determine where she was.The case also involved allegations concerning private communications and personal information. Investigators were particularly interested in how information that appeared in Asea’s online content had been obtained and whether it came from devices or accounts that he was not authorised to access.The allegations formed part of a wider investigation into Asea’s interactions with the women and his use of information in his social-media content.The investigation eventually led authorities to search Asea’s residence and collect electronic equipment for examination. According to court documents described in media reports, investigators seized items including computers, mobile phones, external hard drives, USB storage devices, an iPad, a Dell laptop and other networking equipment.Authorities sought to examine the devices for evidence that could establish how information had been obtained or stored. Investigators were interested in material such as passwords, messages, account information, financial records, browser history and location data. The forensic examination was significant because the allegations involved information that investigators believed may have originated from electronic devices or private accounts.Asea's current case follows an earlier criminal investigation. He was initially arrested in April 2026 in connection with allegations that included stalking and unauthorised computer access. However, prosecutors filed a “No Information” in May, meaning the charges then under consideration were not pursued at that stage.A separate civil proceeding also involved a woman seeking protection through a stalking injunction. A temporary order was issued in July, but the case was later dismissed and the injunction was dissolved in September. The criminal investigation nevertheless returned to court later in the year.On September 24, prosecutors reopened the criminal case and filed a new information against Asea. The revived prosecution focuses on a felony allegation involving unauthorised access to a computer or electronic device. Asea was subsequently booked into the St Lucie County Jail on September 30. His bond was set at $35,000.The current case is narrower than the allegations that surrounded the earlier investigation. The stalking allegations that were previously dropped were not simply reinstated as part of the September filing. Instead, the active criminal charge concerns the alleged unauthorised computer access. Asea is due to appear for arraignment on November 19, according to reports citing court records.
Article Summary: Florida man published more than 100 videos on tik tok. Investigators also examined claims involving location data, purchases and private conversations. Earlier stalking allegations were dropped, but prosecutors revived the computer-related case in september. Asea was booked into the st lucie county jail on september 30 on a felony computer-access charge.
